audits.resolution_reason: No preservation decorations in 1000 sampled inputs; decoration-erasure rival survives synthetic samples but fails lawful Racket-bound witness. Duplicate self_check shadows an earlier contract; no target repair selected.
audits.text:
## 925ec9df8689

**Actionable curriculum defect; no fix applied because this is an audit-only target.**

The audited source hash is
`644088a257034ff1fe2cd81cbee84f4a5fef35ad5100b1a35c016e0e3334cc46`.
The task summary and canonical examples include non-yellow decoration cells
that must be preserved. The generator, however, never paints a decoration: in
250 samples for each of `None`, easy, medium, and hard (1,000 total), every
input palette was a subset of `{0,4}`. The wrong rule “complete each yellow L,
then erase every pre-existing non-0/non-4 cell” therefore disagreed with the
intended rule on 0/1,000 sampled generator inputs.

The minimal 7x7 counterexample has two separated yellow L-windows and a lawful
color-6 decoration at `(3,0)`. It passes the selected `self_check`. The canonical
Racket rule (executed hash `35b7779713e2`) fills the two missing corners with 2
and preserves the 6; the rival changes that 6 to 0. The single differing cell is
recorded as `[3,0,6,0]`.

Evidence and reproducer:
`checks/audit/925ec9df8689/input.json`, `racket.json`,
`rival-output.json`, `probe.py`, `probe.log`, and `report.json`.

Suggested future repair: actually emit 0..2 non-overlapping decoration cells in
colors other than 0/2/4, declare a preservation rival/witness, strengthen
`self_check`, remove the duplicate shadowing `self_check`, and make the public
axis contract exact. Those changes were intentionally not made in this audit.

triage.reason: Retain both source-bound audit reports and reproducers with their target generators. Select individual resolution states explicitly; audit-only targets are not edited.
